function.name: museum_info
function.description: Get information about a museum including its opening hours and ticket prices for a specific date range. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

date.description: The specific date or date range for which information is needed. It could be specific date such as '2022-12-01' or a date range like 'this weekend', 'next week'. It could also be a recurring time such as 'every Saturday'.

information.description: The type of information needed from the museum. This is optional and defaults to 'all' if not specified.

message.reasoning: We need to call the function museum_info with museum="大英博物館" (British Museum), date="this weekend", information="opening_hours,ticket_price"? The function signature says information can be "opening_hours" | "ticket_price" | "address"[]? Actually it's optional and defaults to "all". But we can specify "opening_hours" or "ticket_price" or "address"[]? The type is union of those strings? It says information?: "opening_hours" | "ticket_price" | "address"[], default: "all". So we can pass "opening_hours" or "ticket_price" or "address"[]? But "address"[] seems weird. Maybe they want an array of addresses? But we only need opening hours and ticket price. We can pass "opening_hours" and "ticket_price" separately? The function expects a single string? It says "information?: "opening_hours" | "ticket_price" | "address"[], default: "all"". That means information can be one of those strings or an array of addresses? Actually "address"[] indicates an array of addresses? Might be a mistake. But we can just pass "all" to get both. So call with museum="大英博物館", date="this weekend", information="all".
